commitResults.messageBody: Add the project-specific present-changes-visually skill and its split-view diff generator. Ignore the project Codex skills directory by default while explicitly recording this skill in the repository.

commitResults.messageTitle: Require UI tests after code updates

commitResults.messageBody: Add the delete command with validation, user-friendly confirmation, and task-count updates. Replace the fixed task array with an ArrayList so tasks can be removed cleanly and the remaining tasks are automatically renumbered. Extend the UI test plan with an interleaved deletion test that verifies removal and state preservation.

Introduce TaskType to own task-type display markers and let each task subclass select its type through the base Task class. Remove duplicated marker overrides while preserving existing task behavior and UI output.

Load tasks from data/duke.txt when the chatbot starts and save the complete task list after every mutation. Preserve task types, descriptions, deadlines, event times, and completion states using an OS-independent file path, creating the data directory when necessary.

Validate persisted task records while loading, skip malformed lines without crashing, and report each corrupted line with the supported file formats. Add a manual UI test-plan case covering recovery of valid tasks alongside corrupted records.

Create a backup of the original task file when corruption is detected and write rejected records with line numbers to a separate corrupted-data file. Continue loading valid tasks and document the recovery workflow in the UI test plan.

Use LocalDateTime for deadline and event values instead of raw strings. Accept yyyy-MM-dd and yyyy-MM-dd HHmm input, format dates for display, preserve parsed values during persistence, and report invalid date formats clearly. Document date and time parsing in the UI test plan.

Change deadline, event, and date-filter parsing to accept dd-MM-yyyy and dd-MM-yyyy HHmm by default. Add the list on <date> command to show deadlines and events occurring on a specific date. Update correction messages and UI test-plan examples while retaining LocalDateTime storage and friendly display formatting.

Move mutable task collection ownership and basic add, access, removal, size, and ordered iteration operations out of Daddy. This establishes a focused list abstraction without changing command parsing, persistence, or console output, making the refactor safe to extend in later iterations.

Move task-file paths, loading, saving, record conversion, corrupted-record backup, and corrupt-bin handling out of Daddy into Storage. Daddy now delegates persistence while retaining presentation of returned loading warnings. Read persisted date-times using the ISO representation produced during saving, so dated tasks round-trip across application restarts. Document the valid persisted deadline format and restart check in the UI test plan.

Move greeting, task-list displays, date-filtered displays, task confirmations, errors, and exit formatting from Daddy into Ui. Daddy now supplies Ui with domain data and delegates all System.out calls, keeping command behavior and exact console output unchanged.

Introduce Parser and CommandType to classify user input and extract command arguments. Replace Daddy's long conditional command chain with a command dispatcher that delegates recognition to Parser while preserving existing task operations, validation messages, and command behavior.

Encapsulate task range checks, marking, unmarking, deletion, and date filtering in TaskList. Simplify Daddy's repeated task-number validation through one helper and let Ui render pre-filtered tasks, preserving all existing console behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move task creation parsing into Parser
commitResults.messageBody: Teach Parser to construct todo, deadline, and event tasks from command details, including description validation, delimiter parsing, date-time conversion, and user-facing correction messages. Replace Daddy's separate task-creation methods with one add-and-save workflow for parsed tasks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Centralize command value parsing in Parser
commitResults.messageBody: Move list-date validation and task-number conversion from Daddy into Parser while retaining the task-list range check in Daddy, where the current list size is available. This leaves Daddy as a coordinator across Parser, TaskList, Storage, and Ui without changing command output.

Give Ui ownership of the Scanner and provide readCommand and close methods. Daddy now delegates both console input and output to Ui, leaving it to coordinate Parser, TaskList, Storage, and Ui without changing interactive behavior.

Add an abstract Command execution contract and migrate the bye behavior into ExitCommand. Daddy now executes command objects through a shared helper, establishing the command-pattern foundation while leaving other command paths unchanged for incremental migration.

Add ListCommand and ListOnDateCommand, with Parser constructing the appropriate command from recognized list input and validated dates. Remove list rendering and date-filtering orchestration from Daddy in favor of the shared command execution path.
Add AddCommand to own the add, save, and confirmation workflow for a parsed task. Teach Parser to construct it for todo, deadline, and event commands, removing Daddy's add-specific workflow.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract mark and unmark command objects
commitResults.messageBody: Add dedicated MarkCommand and UnmarkCommand classes that validate a parsed task index, update task status, persist the task list, and show the appropriate confirmation. Teach Parser to construct these commands so Daddy only dispatches them, preserving all existing validation messages and UI behavior.

Add DeleteCommand to validate the selected task index, remove the task, save the list, and display deletion feedback. Move delete command construction into Parser and remove Daddy's remaining task-index mutation workflow.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let Parser create complete command objects
commitResults.messageBody: Introduce Parser.parseCommand as the sole public command-parsing entry point. It now recognizes each input, constructs the appropriate Command, and preserves the existing specific input errors. Simplify Daddy's chat loop to parse once and execute the resulting command, while keeping parsing helpers private implementation details.

Introduce TaskIndexCommand as a common base for commands that operate on one existing task. It stores the parsed index and centralizes range validation, allowing MarkCommand, UnmarkCommand, and DeleteCommand to focus solely on their respective task operations.
Integrate the iterative OOP refactoring that introduces Command subclasses, centralizes command parsing in Parser, and keeps task-index validation shared across task-mutating commands.

Move application classes beneath the daddy package by responsibility: command, exception, parser, storage, task, and ui. Add the required package declarations and imports, and update the UI test plan to compile nested sources and launch daddy.Daddy.

Update the application main class from the starter project's seedu.duke.Duke to the packaged daddy.Daddy entry point, allowing ./gradlew run and generated application artifacts to start the current project.

Use data/daddy.txt as Daddy's current persistence file and migrate a legacy data/duke.txt file when no current file exists. Preserve migrated tasks, explain successful or failed migration to the user, document the behavior in the UI test plan, and ignore runtime data files.

Add complete Javadoc for Daddy's application flow, commands, parser, storage, tasks, UI, exceptions, enums, constructors, and non-obvious fields. Strengthen the project guidance so future classes, enums, constructors, and methods include useful Javadoc tags.

Add JUnit 5 tests for task-list operations, storage persistence and recovery, legacy data migration, and command parsing. Record the ongoing target of testing the highest-value 50 percent of methods and require JUnit test updates after code changes.
Configure Shadow to create an executable fat JAR named Daddy.jar, matching the Daddy application name and bundling runtime dependencies for distribution with java -jar.

Parser error messages exceed the project line-length limit.

Wrap the affected message literals and update the matching unit-test
expectation. This preserves the existing behavior while keeping the code
readable and compliant with the coding standard.

Java code changes need a consistent review process to preserve project
readability and maintainability.

Require the project-specific SE-EDU Java coding-standard skill and its
in-scope audit before Java or test changes are handed over.

Commit quality depends on consistent scope, branch names, and message
formatting.

Require the project-specific SE-EDU Git-standard skill before naming
branches or preparing commits so future history stays clear and useful.

Java and Git changes need consistent project-specific guidance.

Merge the coding-standard branch to require the relevant SE-EDU skills
for future Java work, branch names, and commit preparation. The included
parser formatting cleanup keeps the affected error message within the
project's line-length limit.

Task lists become harder to scan when related tasks are spread across
multiple task types.

Add a case-insensitive find command that displays matching tasks in list
order, with clear feedback for empty queries and no results. Cover the
behavior with unit and UI tests.

Task lists need a quick way to locate related items without manually
scanning every task.

Merge the Level-9 find feature, including case-insensitive matching,
clear empty-query and no-result feedback, and its unit and UI coverage.
Keep the coding-standard formatting in the overlapping parser test.
